title: ShadowKV: KV Cache in Shadows for High-Throughput Long-Context LLM Inference
technique: Low-rank pre-RoPE key cache on GPU plus CPU-offloaded values; landmark-based sparse KV selection and on-the-fly reconstruction of a ~1.56% sparse KV budget; CUDA-graph overlap

optimized_metrics.evidence: We present ShadowKV, a high-throughput long-context LLM inference system that stores the low-rank key cache and offloads the value cache to reduce the memory footprint for larger batch sizes and longer sequences.

an ideal system for long-context LLM inference with sparse attention should: (i) reduce GPU memory usage, (ii) minimize inference latency, and (iii) maintain accuracy within limited sparse KV cache budgets.
To minimize decoding latency, ShadowKV employs an accurate KV selection strategy that reconstructs minimal sparse KV pairs on-the-fly.
(iii) maintain accuracy within limited sparse KV cache budgets.

headline_claim.text: it can support up to 6x larger batch sizes and boost throughput by up to 3.04x on an A100 GPU without sacrificing accuracy

metric_definitions.definition_quote: By measuring the throughput during decoding across different models on A100, we show that ShadowKV can support up to 6x larger batch sizes and boost throughput by up to 3.04x.
metric_definitions.notes: Generation tokens/s during decode only (Table 4 caption 'Generation throughput (tokens/s)'); single A100; prefill excluded; baseline uses the largest batch fitting on GPU.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For the infinite batch size, we leverage A100's theoretical memory bandwidth (2 TB/s) for attention computations.
metric_definitions.notes: Idealized upper bound computed analytically, not measured; ShadowKV claimed to exceed it.

load_regime: offline fixed batch size, context-length sweep (8K-1M), batch maximized per method
tradeoff_acknowledged: Accuracy within ~1.56% degradation on most tasks at 1.56% sparse budget; CPU value fetch latency mitigated by overlap.

extractor_notes: Throughput gain is partly a consequence of larger batch (memory) rather than lower per-token latency; decode-only throughput. The A100 memory size (80GB) was not confirmed in the extracted lines. 'Infinite batch size' is an analytic bound.
